content:
## Meet the Theater

The **Theater** is a 400-by-400-pixel stage where you can create drawings, animations, text, images, and sounds with code.

You control the Theater by calling functions. For example:

* `draw_ellipse()` draws an ellipse or circle.
* `draw_rectangle()` draws a rectangle.
* `pause()` creates a new frame in an animation.
* `play_note()` adds a musical note.
* `play()` displays and plays everything you created.

Import the Theater functions in Python Lab with:

```python
from theater import *
```

You can then call the functions directly:

```python
set_fill_color("blue")
draw_ellipse(150, 150, 100, 100)
play_note(60, 0.5)
pause(0.5)
draw_text("hello", 20, 380)
play()
```

## How the Theater Works

Theater functions record each drawing, animation, and sound action in the order you call them. Call `play()` when you are ready to display the animation and play its soundtrack.

Calling `play()` does not erase your work. If you call it again, the Theater plays the same recording again.

## The Stage and Coordinate System

The stage is always 400 pixels wide and 400 pixels tall. The top-left corner is coordinate `(0, 0)`.

* The `x` coordinate identifies the horizontal position.
* The `y` coordinate identifies the vertical position.
* Moving right increases `x`.
* Moving down increases `y`.
* The center of the stage is `(200, 200)`.

Coordinates do not have to be whole numbers. A drawing can also extend beyond the edge of the stage. The portion outside the stage will not be displayed.

## Drawing Settings

Shapes use the current stroke color, fill color, and stroke width when they are drawn. Changing a setting only affects shapes drawn after the change.

| Setting | Default |
| --- | --- |
| Stroke color | Black |
| Fill color | Black |
| Stroke width | 1 pixel |
| Text color | Black |
| Text height | 20 pixels |
| Font | Sans |
| Font style | Normal |

## Colors

Color functions accept a color name or a hexadecimal color value.

```python
set_fill_color("teal")
set_stroke_color("#4B0082")
```

Color names are not case-sensitive. Available names are:

```text
white      silver     gray       black      red
maroon     yellow     olive      lime       green
aqua       teal       blue       navy       fuchsia
purple     pink       orange     gold       brown
chocolate  tan        turquoise  indigo     violet
beige      ivory
```

Hexadecimal colors can use `#RGB` or `#RRGGBB` format.

## Important Limits

The Theater limits the size of animations and sounds so programs can run smoothly in Python Lab.

| Item | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Animation frames | 600 total frames |
| Pauses | 599 pauses |
| Audio timeline | 300 seconds |
| One sound | 300 seconds |
| `pause()` or note duration | `0.1` to `655.35` seconds |
| MIDI note | `48` to `84` |
| Text height | `1` to `1600` pixels |
| Drawn image width or height | `1` to `4000` pixels |
name: Theater

methods.name: play()
methods.content:
Displays the recorded animation and plays its soundtrack.

Call `play()` after you finish adding drawings, animation frames, and sounds.

methods.name: pause(seconds)
methods.content:
Holds the current picture for a specified number of seconds and then starts a new animation frame.

Everything drawn since the previous `pause()` appears in the frame that the pause completes. A program without `pause()` creates one still picture.

The duration must be between `0.1` and `655.35` seconds.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"seconds","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"How long to display the current frame."}]

methods.name: clear(color)
methods.parameters: [{"name":"color","type":"str","required":true,"description":"A color name or hexadecimal color value."}]
methods.syntax: Fills the entire stage with a color, covering everything that was previously drawn.

methods.name: get_width()
methods.content: Returns the width of the stage. The Theater stage is always `400` pixels wide.

methods.name: get_height()
methods.content: Returns the height of the stage. The Theater stage is always `400` pixels tall.

methods.name: draw_line(start_x, start_y, end_x, end_y)
methods.content: Draws a straight line using the current stroke color and stroke width.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"start_x","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The starting x-coordinate."},{"name":"start_y","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The starting y-coordinate."},{"name":"end_x","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The ending x-coordinate."},{"name":"end_y","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The ending y-coordinate."}]

methods.name: draw_rectangle(x, y, width, height)
methods.content:
Draws a rectangle. `(x, y)` marks the top-left corner of the rectangle.

The width and height cannot be negative.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"x","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The x-coordinate of the top-left corner."},{"name":"y","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The y-coordinate of the top-left corner."},{"name":"width","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The width of the rectangle."},{"name":"height","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The height of the rectangle."}]

methods.name: draw_ellipse(x, y, width, height)
methods.content:
Draws an ellipse inside an imaginary rectangle. `(x, y)` marks the top-left corner of that rectangle, not the center of the ellipse.

Use the same width and height to draw a circle. The width and height cannot be negative.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"x","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The x-coordinate of the top-left corner."},{"name":"y","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The y-coordinate of the top-left corner."},{"name":"width","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The width of the ellipse."},{"name":"height","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The height of the ellipse."}]

methods.name: draw_regular_polygon(x, y, sides, radius)
methods.content:
Draws a polygon with sides of equal length, centered at `(x, y)`.

The `radius` is the distance from the center to each corner. A polygon must have at least three sides.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"x","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The x-coordinate of the polygon's center."},{"name":"y","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The y-coordinate of the polygon's center."},{"name":"sides","type":"int","required":true,"description":"The number of sides. Must be at least `3`."},{"name":"radius","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The distance from the center to each corner."}]

methods.name: draw_shape(points, close)
methods.content:
Draws a shape by connecting a list of coordinate points.

Write the points as one list in the order `[x1, y1, x2, y2, ...]`.

* When `close` is `True`, the last point connects to the first point and the shape is filled.
* When `close` is `False`, the function draws a path of connected lines without filling it.

The list must contain at least two points and an even number of values.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"points","type":"list","required":true,"description":"A list of x- and y-coordinate pairs."},{"name":"close","type":"bool","required":true,"description":"Whether to close and fill the shape."}]

methods.name: set_stroke_color(color)
methods.content: Sets the outline color for shapes drawn after this function is called.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"color","type":"str","required":true,"description":"A color name or hexadecimal color value."}]

methods.name: set_fill_color(color)
methods.content: Sets the interior color for shapes drawn after this function is called.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"color","type":"str","required":true,"description":"A color name or hexadecimal color value."}]

methods.name: set_stroke_width(width)
methods.content:
Sets the outline width for shapes drawn after this function is called.

Stroke width is measured in pixels. A fractional width is rounded, and a value below `1` still produces a 1-pixel line.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"width","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The stroke width in pixels."}]

methods.name: remove_stroke_color()
methods.content: Removes the outline from shapes drawn after this function is called.

methods.name: remove_fill_color()
methods.content: Removes the interior fill from shapes drawn after this function is called.

methods.name: draw_text(text, x, y, rotation=0)
methods.content:
Draws text using the current text color, height, font, and style.

`(x, y)` marks the left end of the text's baseline. The optional rotation is measured in degrees clockwise around `(x, y)`.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"text","type":"str","required":true,"description":"The text to draw."},{"name":"x","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The x-coordinate of the text baseline."},{"name":"y","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The y-coordinate of the text baseline."},{"name":"rotation","type":"int or float","description":"Clockwise rotation in degrees. Defaults to `0`."}]

methods.name: set_text_color(color)
methods.content: Sets the color for text drawn after this function is called.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"color","type":"str","required":true,"description":"A color name or hexadecimal color value."}]

methods.name: set_text_height(height)
methods.content:
Sets the text height in pixels for text drawn after this function is called.

The height must be between `1` and `1600`. The default text height is `20`.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"heigt","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The text height in pixels."}]

methods.name: set_text_style(font, style)
methods.content:
Sets the font and style for text drawn after this function is called.

Available fonts are `"mono"`, `"sans"`, and `"serif"`. Available styles are `"normal"`, `"bold"`, `"italic"`, and `"bold_italic"`.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"font","type":"str","required":true,"description":"The font family: `\"mono\"`, `\"sans\"`, or `\"serif\"`."},{"name":"style","type":"str","required":true,"description":"The font style: `\"normal\"`, `\"bold\"`, `\"italic\"`, or `\"bold_italic\"`."}]

methods.name: draw_image(image, x, y, size=None, width=None, height=None, rotation=0)
methods.content:
Draws an image with its top-left corner at `(x, y)`. The `image` can be the name of an image file in the Python Lab project.

Choose one of these ways to set the image size:

* Use `size` to set the width while keeping the image's original proportions.
* Use both `width` and `height` to stretch the image to an exact size.

Each displayed dimension must be between `1` and `4000` pixels. The optional rotation is measured in degrees clockwise around `(x, y)`.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"image","type":"str or Image","required":true,"description":"An image filename or an `Image`."},{"name":"x","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The x-coordinate of the image's top-left corner."},{"name":"y","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":" The y-coordinate of the image's top-left corner."},{"name":"size","type":"int or float","description":"The image width while preserving its proportions."},{"name":"width","type":"int or float","description":"The exact image width. Use with `height`."},{"name":"height","type":"int or float","description":"The exact image height. Use with `width`."},{"name":"rotation","type":"int or float","description":" Clockwise rotation in degrees. Defaults to `0`."}]

methods.name: play_note(note, seconds, instrument="piano")
methods.content:
Plays a musical note for a specified number of seconds.

The note is a MIDI number from `48` to `84`. MIDI note `60` is middle C, and each step changes the pitch by one semitone.

The available instruments are `"piano"` and `"bass"`. The default instrument is `"piano"`.

`play_note()` does not move the animation clock forward. Notes called without a `pause()` between them begin at the same time and play as a chord.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"note","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"A MIDI note from `48` to `84`."},{"name":"seconds","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The note's duration, from `0.1` to `655.35` seconds."},{"name":"instrument","type":"str","description":"`\"piano\"` or `\"bass\"`. Defaults to `\"piano\"`."}]

methods.name: play_note_and_pause(note, seconds, instrument="piano")
methods.content:
Plays a musical note and pauses the animation for the same amount of time.

This is equivalent to calling `play_note()` followed by `pause()` with the same duration.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"note","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"A MIDI note from `48` to `84`."},{"name":"seconds","type":"int or float","required":true,"description":"The note and pause duration, from `0.1` to `655.35` seconds."},{"name":"instrument","type":"str","description":"`\"piano\"` or `\"bass\"`. Defaults to `\"piano\"`."}]

methods.name: play_sound(sound)
methods.content:
Plays a sound from a WAV file in the Python Lab project or from a list of audio sample values.

A WAV file must use 16-bit PCM audio and cannot be longer than 300 seconds. A list of audio samples must contain numbers from `-1.0` to `1.0` at 44,100 samples per second.

Like `play_note()`, this function does not move the animation clock forward. Use `pause()` to control when later sounds begin.
methods.parameters: [{"name":"sound","type":"str or list","required":true,"description":"A WAV filename or a list of audio sample values."}]
